scientific_question: Can the frozen compact proposal use a minimal native C runtime to preserve the exact downstream inverse result while passing wall and whole-worker RSS gates against the framework-free Zero-K4 reference?
trajectory_role: already-open post-open development fit only; no fresh, validation, or test

adaptation_provenance.trigger: v12.4 passed compatibility, parity, isolation, and wall on p14 but failed whole-worker RSS because MLX added about 50 MB peak memory
adaptation_provenance.permitted_change: replace only the proposal execution backend; weights, architecture, precision boundary, exact lift, alpha, K1, reference, metrics, and gates remain unchanged

backend_selection_before_native_fit_exec.inputs: deterministic synthetic 101x2072 float64 observations and frozen fold-0 checkpoint only
backend_selection_before_native_fit_exec.selection_reason: Pareto choice: proposal median within about 2 percent of batch 32 while synthetic process peak RSS was about 20 MB lower

execution.measured_interval: proposal plus unchanged float64 solver; excludes process startup and one-time loading

decision_rule: all compatibility, parity, isolation, wall, paired-session, and whole-worker RSS gates must pass on p=14kw_size=05; there is no mean-gain override
success_action: authorize the same frozen native backend on the remaining four already-open fit trajectories only
failure_action: freeze the native backend result and stop backend engineering before any fresh, validation, or test access

changing architecture, alpha, solver, reference, metrics, or thresholds
opening p45-s03, validation, or untouched test
